Help

See also: [How To Investigate a Go Test Failure \(internal\)](https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/l/c/HgfXfJgM)

/cc @cockroachdb/jobs [This test on roachdash](https://roachdash.crdb.dev/?filter=status:open%20t:.*TestJobControlByType.*&sort=title+created&display=lastcommented+project) | [Improve this report!](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/tree/master/pkg/cmd/internal/issues) Jira issue: CRDB-25330
comments: @adityamaru  -- mind taking a look at this? Suspect it's the query rewrites that are making this fail.

So I ran the test under stress with @knz's improved debugging output. The test fails in ~100s using `./dev test pkg/jobs -f TestJobControlByType --show-logs --verbose --stream-output --race --stress --stress-args='-p=4' -- --define=tags=bazel,gss,deadlock | tee out;`.

When one of the subtests fails it is the number of affected rows that is usually double what is expected - https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/f59ae77afc7fbd3b1d7eb3448a5b688c659a7958/pkg/jobs/delegate_control_test.go#L482. I verified that the output of `SHOW JOBS` and `TABLE crdb_internal.jobs` are correct and we don't see any duplicate rows in the `system.jobs` table. The error seems to be occurring because the `startExec` method for the `controlJobsNode` is invoked twice https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2f811420a1492ca547659003f193233341b7fd87/pkg/sql/control_jobs.go#L43 causing the number of affected rows to be 2x the expected number of rows. The stack traces for the two calls of `startExec` aren't all that different.

I haven't yet been able to figure out why we occasionally see two calls to `startExec`, but nothing seems wrong with the output of the underlying job system.

Looks like every time the test fails, we have an automatic stats job running in between the subtest. This is somehow causing `startExec` to be called twice. Disabling automatic stats collection seems to deflake the test. It has been running for 20mins without failure.

> The error seems to be occurring because the startExec method for the controlJobsNode is invoked twice https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2f811420a1492ca547659003f193233341b7fd87/pkg/sql/control_jobs.go#L43 causing the number of affected rows to be 2x the expected number of rows

So even with a regular SQL internal retry the NumRowsAffected should be reset to 0 between retries.
If confirmed this would be a major SQL exec bug.

@yuzefovich do you have some suggestions?
I plan to dig some more this morning so I'll post here if I find anything new.

Hm, two stacks correspond to different plans (i.e. `controlJobsNode`s in two stacks should be totally independent of each other - they have different memory addresses), so I don't see how rows affected number from one execution would affect another.

It's interesting to note that in the first stack we had execution stats collection enabled (probably because the stmt was "sampled" - it might be an interesting experiment to try modifying `sql.txn_stats.sample_rate` setting to see whether the likelihood of the flake changes).

I don't think I'm any closer to understanding the root cause but I have some more information that I'm dumping here incase you see something @yuzefovich.

Our test uses `ExecEx` to run the job control query. This query is of the form `PAUSE ALL RESTORE JOBS` but the failure happens at random control queries so this is not related to the pausing of the restore jobs. We assert that the number of rows affected is equal to the number of jobs that we expect to make a state transition. This number is returned by `ExecEx` and is incremented here - https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9d4a2a1b831a57deb21656b5ffcb12dfd3b9100f/pkg/sql/internal.go#L433

I added log lines in a few places and I see that we're incrementing the row count twice in `handleDataObject`. First, because of a call from https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9d4a2a1b831a57deb21656b5ffcb12dfd3b9100f/pkg/sql/internal.go#L462 and the second time because of a call from https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9d4a2a1b831a57deb21656b5ffcb12dfd3b9100f/pkg/sql/internal.go#L470

Walking further up the stack I see two calls to `IncrementRowsAffected` from https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6eff5ce861ae903c6867d71bec475c806bfb1893/pkg/sql/distsql_running.go#L1435 which is what feeds into the above calls to `handleDataObject`. The two calls to `IncrementRowsAffected` is what results in the number of rows being double what we expect.

> it might be an interesting experiment to try modifying sql.txn_stats.sample_rate setting to see whether the likelihood of the flake changes

I'll try doing this next
Setting `sql.txn_stats.sample_rate` to 0 did not affect the flakiness of the test. The only _reliable_ way I have seen the flake go away is by disabling automatic stats generation.

Spoke to @yuzefovich offline and we think this is a legitimate bug in how the `ieResultWriter` accumulates data but does not reset between retries. Yahor has a fix in mind so reassigning this issue to him.
